land.text: the Croatian, Bosnian and Syrmian lands of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, taken in the Axis invasion of April 1941

predecessors.note: The Axis invasion began on 6 April 1941; the NDH was proclaimed in Zagreb on 10 April, a week before the Yugoslav surrender of 17 April.

land.text: the Yugoslavia of the Partisans, which took the NDH territory in 1944-1945

successors.note: The NDH government was dissolved on 8 May 1945 (infobox); the Yugoslav Partisans dossier names the same successor.

capitals.name: Zagreb
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital and largest city: Zagreb'; 'On 10 April 1941 the German army took control in Zagreb.'

rulers.name: Ante Pavelić
rulers.title: Poglavnik (leader)
rulers.note: Slavko Kvaternik proclaimed the state on 10 April 1941 'in the name of ... the poglavnik Ante Pavelić'; Pavelić returned to Zagreb on 15 April and 'took power as Poglavnik on 16 April 1941'. The page also has a figurehead king, Aimone, Duke of Aosta, under the 15 May 1941 laws of the Crown of Zvonimir, who is not listed as a ruler.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1941 shape without Trogir, for 18 May 1941 to 10 September 1943: the NDH after the Treaties of Rome, holding the Dalmatian hinterland (Knin, Drniš, Sinj, Imotski, Makarska, Metković, Senj) and not the annexed coast and islands; Trogir is Italian in the Governorate of Dalmatia (Spalato province)

keyframe_review.note: 96,150 km2 against the infobox's 115,133 km2 for 1941 (ratio 0.84, within a factor of two). The shape already lacks the coast and islands that the Treaties of Rome of 18 May 1941 gave Italy ('Italy annexed a significant central portion of Dalmatia and various Adriatic Islands'): a point test puts Split, Šibenik, Zadar, Korčula, Mljet, Krk and Rab outside it and Knin, Drniš, Sinj, Imotski, Makarska, Metković and Senj inside (28 of the 48 Dalmatian cells). So the first draft's removal of all Dalmatia was wrong and is withdrawn; the shape is kept, and only Trogir, which it holds but Governorate_of_Dalmatia places in the Spalato province (annexed), is taken out. Not done: Brač, Hvar and Dubrovnik, which the shape lacks, are on that page 'not formally annexed' (occupied by Italy, Dubrovnik under Pavelić's 'nominal control'); they are left outside the shape and outside the Italian loss because the occupation is undated ('after the autumn of 1941') and has no Italian-side event, a gap for the gap-filler. The April-May 1941 NDH is carried by the found event.

78,716 km2 against 96,150 km2 in 1941. The shape lacks 64 cells of the 1943 shape (Lika, Kordun, Una-Sana, parts of Herzegovina and the Dalmatian hinterland) and so suits the pages' 'The Partisan movement was soon able to control a large percentage of the NDH' and the Partisans 'effectively controlled the entire eastern half of Yugoslavia - and most of the Dalmatian coast' by late 1944; the pages give no figures, so the boundary is Cliopatria's. Dalmatia is taken out in December 1944 (ledger).

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1944 shape without the 18 Dalmatian cells it still holds (Sinj, Imotski, Makarska, Trogir and the hinterland), which the Partisans took in December 1944 (ledger); the NDH of January 1945, before Mostar and Sarajevo fell and the Syrmian front broke

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no shape for 1945 (the infobox gives 'Government dissolved: 8 May 1945', 'Armed Forces surrender: 15 May 1945'). The state in January 1945 is the 1944 shape less the Dalmatian cells that shape still holds (18 of the 1944 shape's cells lie in the Dalmatia region: the hinterland, not the coast, which Italy took out of the 1941 shape), the land the Partisans took by 'late 1944' ('most of the Dalmatian coast', ledger /ledger/10); the Germans left Mostar on 12 February and Sarajevo on 15 April, which the ledger removes.

region.text: Croatia without Međimurje, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Syrmia: the Cliopatria 1941 shape

ledger.note: 10 April 1941: the Independent State of Croatia is proclaimed at Zagreb. 'On 10 April 1941 the German army took control in Zagreb'; Slavko Kvaternik proclaimed it 'in the name of Croats and the header (poglavnik) Ante Pavelić.' Its territory 'consisted mostly of modern-day Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as some parts of modern-day Serbia and Slovenia', 'the whole of Bosnia and Herzegovina' and 'the whole of Syrmia'; 'Međimurje and southern Baranja were annexed by the Kingdom of Hungary', which the NDH disputed.

10 April 1941: the NDH is a German client from its birth. 'It was a protectorate of Fascist Italy from 1941 to 1943, and a puppet state of Nazi Germany from 1941 to 1945.' Roles reversed: the NDH is the client of the counterpart (nazi-germany records the same relation from its side, /ledger/28 and /ledger/82). The page also divides the state 'into German and Italian zones' (1941-1943) and, after Italy's capitulation, 'the German zone of influence was expanded to the whole Independent State of Croatia'.

region.text: the Dalmatian coast and islands outside the Cliopatria 1941 shape (Split, Šibenik, Korčula, Mljet, Šolta and the rest of the Split and Šibenik coast), Trogir, and the Kvarner islands Krk and Rab; not Zadar, Brač, Hvar, Pag or Dubrovnik, and not the Bay of Kotor (never NDH land)

ledger.note: 18 May 1941: the Treaties of Rome give Italy the Dalmatian coast and islands. 'On 18 May, the Treaties of Rome were signed by diplomats of the NDH and Italy'; 'Nevertheless, Italy annexed a significant central portion of Dalmatia and various Adriatic Islands' (Split and Šibenik named; 'nearly all Croatian Adriatic islands, including Rab, Krk, Vis, Korčula, Mljet'; 'some smaller areas such as the Bay of Kotor'). The region is my reading: the Cliopatria 1941 shape already lacks this coast and these islands (it holds the hinterland: Knin, Sinj, Imotski, Makarska, Metković, Senj), so the loss is Dalmatia outside the shape plus Trogir, which the shape holds but Governorate_of_Dalmatia puts in the Spalato province, plus Krk and Rab, which that page says were 'administratively united to the Italian province of Fiume'. Left out: Pag (in the shape), Brač and Hvar ('occupied by the Italian army' but 'not formally annexed to the Governorate'), Dubrovnik (Mussolini 'was temporarily stopped by the strong opposition of Pavelić, who retained nominal control') and Zadar (Italian before the war; the NDH tried to annex Zara in 1943 and Germany refused). The Bay of Kotor was never NDH land (kingdom-of-italy records it from yugoslavia). Second page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governorate_of_Dalmatia.

1941: Italian protectorate over the NDH. The page: 'a protectorate of Fascist Italy from 1941 to 1943'. The page gives the years only; the month is the Treaties of Rome (18 May 1941), which is my reading. Roles reversed: the NDH is the client of the counterpart; the Kingdom of Italy dossier has no matching event yet (request in notes).

4 November 1942: the Partisans take Bihać. They 'took Bihać and neighbouring towns on 4 November 1942', setting up the Bihać Republic 'in the heart of the NDH'. Recorded as a loss (the Partisans hold the town) to agree with yugoslav-partisans /ledger/4, replacing the contest of the first draft.

29 January 1943: Axis forces retake Bihać. Operation Weiss began 'on 20 January' 1943 and 'Germans entered it on 29 January without a fight'; Drvar fell on 28 February and Livno on 5 March. The date is the page's; Una-Sana as the land of the Bihać Republic is my reading. Matches yugoslav-partisans /ledger/5, which has the year only. The page says the 1st Croatian and 1st Bosnian Corps later reclaimed most of their territory; the Cliopatria 1943 shape and this dossier do not follow that.

region.text: the Dalmatian coast and islands ceded in 1941 (Split, Šibenik, Trogir and the islands of the Spalato and Zara provinces), without Zadar and without Krk and Rab

ledger.note: 10 September 1943: the NDH takes back the ceded coast. 'On 8 September 1943, Italy capitulated and the NDH officially considered the Treaties of Rome to be void', and on 10 September it 'annexed the portion of Dalmatia that had been ceded to Italy'; 'the NDH acquired control of northern Dalmatia (Split and Šibenik)'; Germany did not allow the annexation of Zara (Zadar). The Axis occupation page: the Governorate of Dalmatia was dissolved and 'its territories were split between Germany and the NDH', so Krk and Rab are not regained here (kingdom-of-italy /ledger/38 hands the whole annexation to nazi-germany). 'By 1943, most of the ceded Dalmatian territory was controlled by the Partisans', so the control is a claim in part.

8 September 1943: Italy capitulates and the protectorate ends ('a protectorate of Fascist Italy from 1941 to 1943'; 'On 8 September 1943, Italy capitulated'). The NDH stays a German client, the German zone now covering the whole state.

region.text: the land the Cliopatria NDH holds in 1943 and no longer in 1944: Lika, Kordun, Una-Sana, parts of Herzegovina and the Dalmatian hinterland, the Partisan-held interior

ledger.note: 1944: the Partisan-held interior. Cliopatria's NDH shrinks from 96,150 to 78,716 km2; the page says the Partisans 'effectively controlled the entire eastern half of Yugoslavia - and most of the Dalmatian coast' by late 1944 but gives no dated boundary. The year is Cliopatria's. The Yugoslav Partisans dossier records the same land as a gain. Reopened in the repair pass: the Yugoslav Partisans page gives only the late-1944 control of 'the entire eastern half of Yugoslavia' and no dated gain inside the NDH, so the year stays Cliopatria's (confidence 1).

region.text: Syrmia, where the front froze in winter 1944-45

ledger.note: Winter 1944-1945: the Syrmian Front. 'The Wehrmacht and the forces of the Ustaše-controlled NDH fortified a front in Syrmia that held through the winter of 1944-45'.

intersect.text: most of Dalmatia and nearly all the Adriatic islands

region.text: the Dalmatian coast still inside the 1944 shape

ledger.note: Late 1944: the Partisans hold most of the Dalmatian coast. 'By this time the Partisans effectively controlled the entire eastern half of Yugoslavia - and most of the Dalmatian coast'; the Yugoslav Partisans dossier has a Dalmatia gain in winter 1944.
12 February 1945: the Germans leave Mostar. The page: 'Germans left Mostar on 12 February'; the Partisans take the city. Matching event missing in yugoslav-partisans (request in notes).

region.text: Syrmia, where the front froze in winter 1944-45

ledger.note: March 1945: the Partisan side of the Syrmian contest passes to the new state. 'On 8 March 1945, a coalition Yugoslav government was formed in Belgrade with Tito as Premier'; the yugoslav-partisans dossier dissolves into yugoslavia in March 1945 (/ledger/16). The front itself stays frozen until April; the contest continues with yugoslavia.

region.text: Syrmia, where the front froze in winter 1944-45

ledger.note: March 1945: the Syrmian Front continues against the Yugoslavia of the 8 March coalition government. The page: the Wehrmacht and NDH forces 'fortified a front in Syrmia that held through the winter of 1944-45'. The yugoslavia dossier has no Syrmian contest yet (request in notes).

15 April 1945: the Germans leave Sarajevo. The page: Germans 'did not leave Sarajevo until 15 April'; the Yugoslav Partisans page has the Partisans 'taking Sarajevo in early April' (days apart, same month). The Partisans dossier had dissolved in March 1945 (yugoslav-partisans /ledger/16), so the counterpart is yugoslavia, whose 1945 gain of the NDH (/ledger/25) has no month.

region.text: Syrmia, where the front froze in winter 1944-45

ledger.note: Mid-April 1945: the Syrmian Front ends. The page says the Germans 'held their own until mid-April' in the open country west of Belgrade but does not describe the front breaking. Counterpart yugoslavia after the Partisans' merger of March 1945.

8 May 1945: the NDH government is dissolved ('a puppet state of Nazi Germany from 1941 to 1945'; infobox 'Government dissolved: 8 May 1945'); nazi-germany /ledger/82 records the end from its side. The client ends with its patron.

union.text: most of Dalmatia and nearly all the Adriatic islands

region.text: the land still held in spring 1945: Zagreb, Slavonia, Syrmia and northern Bosnia

ledger.note: 8 May 1945: the NDH government is dissolved. Infobox 'Government dissolved: 8 May 1945' and 'Armed Forces surrender: 15 May 1945'; 'On 25 May 1945, the final battle of the Second World War in Europe, the Battle of Odžak, ended the state'. The land passes to the Yugoslavia of the Partisans.

wars.name: Invasion of Yugoslavia
wars.outcome: Yugoslavia partitioned: the NDH proclaimed on 10 April 1941, the war ended 'with the unconditional surrender signed by General Danilo Kalafatović on 17 April'; Hungary took Vojvodina, Baranja, Bačka and Međimurje and Italy took Dalmatian land.
wars.note: Invasion began on 6 April 1941; the NDH was 'ratified under the Treaties of Rome' on 18 May.

wars.name: World War II in Yugoslavia

zones.text: Syrmia, where the front froze in winter 1944-45
Dalmatia: the coast Italy annexed in 1941 and the hinterland the Partisans took in 1944

wars.outcome: The Partisans take the interior, the Dalmatian coast and Bosnia in 1944-1945 and the NDH government dissolves on 8 May 1945.
wars.note: Bihać Republic 4 November 1942 to 29 January 1943; Syrmian Front winter 1944-45; Mostar 12 February and Sarajevo 15 April 1945.

certainty.note: A puppet state split into German and Italian zones by an undated line of demarcation, with the interior held by the Partisans from 1942; only the Dalmatian line of the Treaties of Rome of 18 May 1941 and the Hungarian annexation line are treaty lines, and the pages name no coordinates.

notes:
Page budget (1-2) exceeded: the first draft opened three pages (NDH article, Axis occupation of Yugoslavia, World War II in Yugoslavia); the repair pass added Governorate of Dalmatia, Battle of the Neretva and Yugoslav Partisans because the reviewer's blocking findings were about the Dalmatian region, the vassal relations and the Bihać dates.

Cliopatria problems: (1) the 1941 shape (to 1943) already lacks the Italian-annexed coast and islands (first draft wrongly removed all of Dalmatia; withdrawn), holds Trogir (Spalato province, annexed) and lacks Brač, Hvar and Dubrovnik (occupied, not formally annexed); (2) there is no 1945 shape although the state lasted to 8 May 1945; (3) the 1944 loss is dated by Cliopatria only; (4) it holds 20 percent of South Bačka (Južno-Backi) and 77 percent of Serbian Srem while excluding Međimurje and, for the most part, southern Baranja, the lands Hungary annexed; the pages do not tell which parts of Bačka and Baranja went to Hungary, so the shape stands.

Vassal events: the NDH carries vassal_start/vassal_end against nazi-germany (1941-4 to 1945-5) and kingdom-of-italy (1941-5 to 1943-9) with the roles reversed (the counterpart is the patron; the patron's own dossier names the NDH as the vassal). A renderer must read them as mirrors of nazi-germany /ledger/28 and /82 and not tint the NDH twice.

Not settled: the German-Italian line of demarcation inside the state (undated on the three pages that mention it, so no occupation event); the Kingdom of Croatia monarchy of 15 May 1941 (a figurehead; no territorial event); the Italian occupation of Pag, Brač, Hvar and Dubrovnik (dated 'after autumn 1941' at best; no Italian-side event); the Hungarian annexation of Međimurje and southern Baranja (undated on every page opened, so no event; hungarian-republic /ledger/20 holds the 1944 loss to yugoslavia); the Partisan gains of 1944 inside the NDH (year only).

Counterparts: kingdom-of-italy /ledger/25 and /38 take the Dalmatian annexation from yugoslavia and give it to nazi-germany in 1943-9, while this dossier names kingdom-of-italy as the party of the cession and return; yugoslav-partisans has Bihać as gain 1942-11 and loss 1943, matching this dossier's loss 1942-11 and gain 1943-1. Zadar is used as a place; Mostar, Sarajevo, Dubrovnik, Dalmatia, Una-Sana, Sremski and Vukovarsko-Srijemska resolve. Trogir, Krk and Rab are not in the gazetteer and are written as coordinates.
